title: OMP2HMPP: Compiler Framework for Energy-Performance Trade-off Analysis of Automatically Generated Codes
review_status: full-text audit complete; transformation and search pipeline, PolyBench evaluation, platform, energy boundary, reported metrics and exponential configuration limitation checked
sections_checked: Variant generation and combinatorial search limitation
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2015-06-09; International Journal of Computer Science Issues 12(2), March 2015 (as printed in the paper)
evidence_note: On selected PolyBench kernels and one dual-CPU/dual-GPU blade, the paper reports 31x average speedup and 5.86x operations/watt relative to its OpenMP baseline. Energy excludes chassis components outside the blade. Search is limited to at most 21 variants per simple block and can grow exponentially with multiple blocks.

title: Introducing ReQuEST: an Open Platform for Reproducible and Quality-Efficient Systems-ML Tournaments
review_status: full-text audit complete; proposed tournament/workflow design, live-scoreboard proof of concept, aspiration versus demonstrated outcomes and future work checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2018-01-19; related invited-talk abstract listed for EMC2 2018; this audit treats the arXiv text as a platform proposal with a proof-of-concept, not a controlled outcome evaluation
evidence_note: The paper proposes common workflows and tournaments for systems-ML quality/efficiency comparisons, shows a live scoreboard proof of concept, and describes broader standardization and platform coverage as goals. It does not experimentally establish reduced reproducibility variance or rank bias.

title: The Weak Call-By-Value λ-Calculus is Reasonable for Both Time and Space
review_status: full-text audit complete; formal theorem assumptions, weak call-by-value strategy, Boolean output restriction, asymptotic time/space overheads, Coq scope and implementation caveat checked
sections_checked: Sections 2–6: simulation strategies and overhead results
Related/future work and canonical implementation caveat
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2019-02-20; peer-reviewed POPL 2020, Proceedings of the ACM on Programming Languages 4 (POPL), Article 27
evidence_note: Proves polynomial time and constant-factor space simulation overhead for deterministic weak call-by-value λ-calculus under natural β-step/maximum-term-size measures, for Boolean-valued functions with T,S in Ω(n). Coq formalization covers sections 2–3. The authors explicitly do not claim a uniform canonical implementation.
